title: Dualizing complexes after finite coefficient extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be Noetherian, and let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] be dualizing: $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] preserves that category and its evaluation-transpose biduality maps are isomorphisms. For every commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra $A$, put $K_A=A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For general $A$, bounded constructible means bounded cohomology admitting a finite locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely generated $A$-module stalks; finite Tor amplitude means that derived tensor with every $A$-module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology in one fixed finite interval. Then $K_A$ is bounded constructible and $R\mathcal Hom_A(-,K_A)$ preserves the bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, with natural isomorphisms given by their evaluation-transpose biduality maps. In particular, when $A$ is a finite field, this applies to all of $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. For $N\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the canonical internal-Hom base-change identifications for $A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}N$ identify its biduality map with $A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(N\to D_KD_KN)$.
